title: Discovery Hit Triage Assistant
short: Ranks screening hits by potency, selectivity, ADMET flags and prior evidence so chemists focus on the most promising series.
symptom: Too many screening hits, too little time to judge them
ingredient: A triage assistant for medicinal chemists
directions: Upload the hit list with assay results. Get a ranked shortlist with liability flags and linked prior evidence for the project team.
problem: A screening campaign produces hundreds of hits; deciding which to pursue means cross-checking assay data, structural alerts, predicted ADMET properties and published activity by hand.
why: Choosing the wrong series wastes months of chemistry and assay resources before the problem becomes clear.
solution: Combines assay results with predicted ADMET and toxicity alerts and with known activity from public bioactivity databases, then ranks hits and explains each score so chemists can challenge it.
limitations: Predicted ADMET values are estimates with known error ranges
Models trained on public data may not fit novel chemistry
review: Medicinal chemists and biologists decide which series advance; scores only support discussion.
